//: Data for `python tools/deploy.py`. Each artifact names where it is built,
//1: where it goes in a live install, and the literal strings that MUST be
//2: present in the built file. A marker is a feature's fingerprint: if the
//3: string is gone, the feature is gone, and the deploy is refused.
//4: Markers must be literals the compiler cannot fold away -- log message
//5: text is ideal, because it is emitted verbatim and it names the feature.
//6: Add a marker the same day you add a feature; that is the whole point.
//7: An artifact may also declare the DATA it needs, with `data`. The file
//8: list is DERIVED by walking `src` -- never enumerated here, because a
//9: hardcoded list rots the day someone adds a data file. `exclude` uses
//10: the same set `aowl payload`/`stageTarkovData` already established:
//11: `capture/**` is a recording of the real backend kept to check this
//12: server AGAINST, not anything it serves (690 files, mostly regenerated
//13: rather than stored, so a payload built on one machine would carry it
//14: and one built on another would not) -- skipped by NAME, not by size,
//15: because large is not the reason. `*.md` is documentation. `minFiles`
//16: is a floor that makes the derivation falsifiable: a glob that silently
//17: matches almost nothing FAILS instead of passing with an empty set.
//gen: generatedSources: files the BUILD WRITES that sit inside a source
//gen1: root. tools/buildlock.py's post-build staleness check must not treat
//gen2: one as an input: symTab() in tools/aowl.nim regenerates these before
//gen3: anything compiles, so they are newer than the artifact after EVERY
//gen4: build, and two no-op `build host` runs exited 6 ARTIFACT STALE on
//gen5: 2026-09-02 naming aowlspt_symtab.nim. Adding an entry here WEAKENS a
//gen6: check -- a real source listed here would read as UP-TO-DATE forever
//gen7: -- so add one only for a file a build step demonstrably writes.
//gen8: The key is `path`, NOT `src`: aowl.nim's deployArtifacts reader is
//gen9: line-based and would treat a `src` line here as an artifact to build.

//d10: flagDefaultsOn -- D10's allowlist, read by tools/flagaudit.py (not
//d10a: by deploy.py). Every `readBoolKeyDef("name", true)` in host/ must be
//d10b: here with the reason it ships ON; anything else FAILS the build before
//d10c: the lock. Same rule as the markers below: NEVER add an entry to make a
//d10d: check pass. An entry whose site no longer defaults true is reported
//d10e: stale. Populated 2026-09-03 from the five sites that already existed;
//d10f: each reason is quoted from the comment at that site, not invented.

flagDefaultsOn.uiShowEvents: The mod-facing `ui.show` event bus. It adds NO new detour: it wants the same byte-verified uihooks show sites the in-host subscribers already bind, never site 1 (MenuScreen::Awake, which killed the client on three boots), and its per-firing cost is one small JSON string on a screen open -- not per frame. It must default ON because arming happens ONCE, before any mod has loaded: a mod cannot subscribe in time to cause its own site to bind, so default OFF would make whether a site is bound depend on mod load order. With it off a mod can still ASK (aowlspt.host::ui_show_status, whose `flag` field reports false) but is never told.
flagDefaultsOn.catchErrorDialogs: Reads only: three read-only postfix detours on prologue-verified, offline-UNIQUE targets, two VirtualQuery-guarded string hops under the guard, one log line, and the original always runs. Default OFF would make the default configuration the one where an unattended run that hits an error dialog reports IDLE and burns its whole timeout.
flagDefaultsOn.modLoadScreen: The in-game mod loading screen. It writes nothing to the game, installs no detour, and builds nothing until the compile writes its file, so on an install whose mods are already built it is inert. It exists to make a long silent wait legible, and a screen you have to switch on does not do that.
flagDefaultsOn.deferModLoad: Gated by modLoadScreen (`gModLoad and readBoolKeyDef(...)`), so it cannot be on while the screen it belongs to is off. Same shipping decision as modLoadScreen.
flagDefaultsOn.forceOfflinePractice: Forces the Matchmaker Offline Raid Screen's practice/offline toggle ON (Toggle::set_isOn @0x55BA430) so a raid entered by pressing straight through the menus stays OFFLINE and never enters the online NetworkGameMatching that times out and crashes the load. Default OFF means the automated raid path is the crashing one.
flagDefaultsOn.nativeTabsSubtabs: The shipping PostFX subtab path. It has a live PASS -- exactly one subtab reads m_IsOn=1 and its panel is the only active one of the two, with the stock SettingsList byte-identical to the feature-off baseline -- and it replaces the cloned-strip approach.
flagDefaultsOn.settingsNativePostFx: The POSTFX subtab's NATIVE rows, which drive the GAME'S OWN post-processing and shading. It defaults ON because it REPLACES rather than adds: `settingsPostFxRows` (mods/graphics, our own D3D composite pass) is now LEGACY and default OFF, so shipping the replacement off as well would leave the POSTFX page EMPTY, which reads to a player as a removed feature. What it arms is not a new risk surface: NO DETOUR IS BOUND ANYWHERE by this feature. Every one of its twelve targets is a DIRECT CALL at a 16-byte prologue verified against the startup snapshot (abi/aowlspt_nativepostfx.h), all MEASURED UNIQUE (owners=1) and in the `il2cpp` section, and its only store into game memory (PrismEffects' three AO fields) goes through the typed hostfieldwrite gate whose klass admission refuses a wrong-klass receiver. It is inert unless BOTH settingsPostFxSubtab and nativeUiKit are on, and it refuses to arm otherwise with a named warning. Idle cost off the settings screen is one boolean test; nothing runs per frame in a raid. The one genuinely expensive knob -- shadow quality, which re-renders the shadow map -- is behind its OWN flag `settingsNativeShadows`, DEFAULT OFF. The one managed-throw hazard on the path (CameraManager::SetSharpen raises a managed NullReferenceException on a null _ccSharpen@0xD0, MEASURED by disassembly, and SEH cannot catch that) is handled by reading and null-checking that field first, with the C wrapper demanding the pointer as an argument so the check cannot be skipped.
